Discovery and rediscovery

Read an appliance's entire configuration in one read-only sweep, refresh SATOM's cache and inventory from it, and optionally capture the full policy depth and the CLI configuration.

👤 ForOperatorAdministrator
🔑 Permissionsappliances.view appliances.apply backups.create backups.restore
📍 WhereAppliances → (device) → Appliance Actions → Discovery / Rediscovery (URL /appliances/<id>/rediscover)

What is it?#

Discovery (the first time) or Rediscovery (every time after) is a single read-only pass that asks a FortiWeb or FortiADC for every configuration object SATOM knows how to read. The result becomes the device's latest configuration snapshot, refreshes SATOM's local cache and fills in the appliance's model, firmware and interfaces. Two optional passes can follow: a deep capture (FortiWeb: every server policy and web-protection profile; FortiADC: every child table), and a CLI capture of show full-configuration over SSH.

What does it do?#

  • Sends a GET to every top-level configuration endpoint in the endpoint registry (FortiADC: the FortiADC discovery plan). Sub-tables that need a parent key are skipped; the Policy Inspector / VS Inspector and the deep capture cover those.
  • Classifies every answer: ok (the device answered — an empty list really is empty), absent (this firmware does not serve the path) or error (anything else).
  • Writes a configuration snapshot, and keeps one copy per firmware version so an upgrade never overwrites the evidence of the previous version.
  • Feeds the local cache as a harvest (trigger rediscovery), so Device health and the configuration pages read from it.
  • Records the running firmware on the appliance.
  • After the sweep, fills in the physical inventory once per snapshot: adds new interfaces, refreshes their type and IP, and sets the model and Hardware/VM type. It never deletes interfaces and never overwrites the role, segment, connected to, notes or datasheet you entered.
  • Keeps up to 3 reads in flight per FortiWeb, on one reused connection pool, in the endpoint sweep and in the deep pass alike. FortiADC is read one request at a time.
  • Runs as a background job, visible in the Jobs dock, on the Jobs page and on the device's Jobs on this device card. A sweep can be stopped.
  • Hardware facts (CPU, memory, disks) are not collected here: use Scan hardware (SSH) on Device health.

Requirements#

  • An appliance of kind FortiWeb or FortiADC. The deep capture differs per product: policy and WPP depth on FortiWeb, every child table on FortiADC.
  • Working credentials. On FortiWeb and FortiADC a credential failure stops the sweep at once (see Troubleshooting).
  • For the CLI capture: SSH access to the device with the same credentials, and permission to write to the configuration vault.

Permissions#

Action Permission
Open the page and follow the progress appliances.view
Start discovery / Start rediscovery, Stop appliances.apply
Tick Also capture the CLI configuration appliances.apply plus backups.create or backups.restore, because the dump is stored in the configuration vault

🔑Permission — Without the permission

A user with only appliances.view can open the page; pressing Start shows Server error 403 — check permissions or try refreshing. A user without a backups permission sees the CLI switch disabled with the reason the CLI dump is written to the configuration vault, which this user may not write. If the CLI flag is posted anyway, the sweep starts without it and the page says CLI capture not started: followed by that reason.

How to use#

Run a sweep#

  1. Open the appliance's page and click Discovery (binoculars icon) or Rediscovery (arrows icon) under Appliance Actions. In the appliance list the same icon is on each FortiWeb and FortiADC row.
  2. The page shows the last sweep (time, objects, sections), whether policy depth has been captured (Depth captured: … or Depth: not captured) and the last CLI dump (CLI dump: … or CLI dump: none captured).
  3. Optionally switch on: - Capture full WPP + policy depth (slow) — FortiWeb. On a FortiADC the switch reads Capture full depth: every child table (REST) (slower); see FortiADC depth capture. - Re-read predefined WPPs in full — FortiWeb only, and only used together with the depth switch. See Predefined WPPs and the factory catalog. - Also capture the CLI configuration (SSH, slow).
  4. Click Start discovery (or Start rediscovery).
  5. Follow the Progress card. While the sweep runs it reads 42/310 endpoints · 1250 objects · Server Policy. Endpoint errors are grouped by reason underneath, for example 3 endpoint error(s): with up to three reasons.
  6. When it is done, the line summarises the result: 1250 object(s) across 18 section(s) from 310 endpoint(s), 12 absent, 3 error(s), followed by the outcome of the optional passes.

Deep capture with progress#

With Capture full WPP + policy depth (slow) on, after the sweep SATOM walks every server policy and web-protection profile (WPP) — sub-tables, rule lists, disabled signatures, exceptions — plus certificates and SNI, and stores the result as the device's deep layer. This is what the Analysis pages and the policy detail pages read.

The WPPs are walked first, and every device read goes through a memo that lasts for the sweep: a server policy that names a WPP already walked is answered from the memo instead of reading that WPP's subtree again. The captured configuration is the same as with a full re-read.

The progress bar switches to the deep pass's own count and names what it is walking:

  • Deep capture: listing server policies and WPPs… — before the lists are read.
  • Deep capture 12/40 · 25 server policies, 15 WPPs · server policy 12/25: www-shop — walking one object, out of how many.
  • … · certificates and SNI and … · saving — the last phases.

While predefined WPPs are being rebuilt from the factory catalog, the line also shows · 18 predefined WPP(s) from the factory catalog, and while a CLI capture runs at the same time it shows · CLI capture running alongside.

When it finishes, the result line adds depth: 900 object(s) from 25 server policies and 15 WPPs (1840 device reads, 610 reused): how many reads went to the device and how many the memo answered. If the deep pass fails, the sweep itself still counts: the line adds depth error: and the reason.

FortiADC depth capture#

On a FortiADC the switch is Capture full depth: every child table (REST). After the sweep, SATOM reads each registered <parent>_child_<table> table once per parent object of the sweep (?pkey=<parent>). The members of certificate groups, CA groups, intermediate-CA groups and schedule groups exist only in these child tables; the parent rows do not carry them. A child table the build does not serve is asked once, recorded as absent, and not asked again for the other parents. A path that changes the device on a GET is never read.

The progress line reads Deep capture 12/40 child-table reads · <table> ← <parent>, and the result line adds depth: 120 child row(s) from 40 child-table reads (plus , N error(s) when reads failed).

The capture feeds three places:

  • The VS Inspector — From last rediscovery draws the virtual-server trees from the sweep and this capture (see FortiADC workspace).
  • The cache's deep layer, as FortiWeb's depth capture does. Every parent of a child table this build serves (pools, certificate groups, content routing and rewriting, schedule groups…) is stored with the rows read for it, as <parent>/<child> under the parent. Where the child table answered rows, the copy of the same members the parent embeds is left out, so a pool member is never counted twice. Analysis reads this layer: the FortiADC object (child tables) drill-down, the sub-element counts, the fleet inventory and the FortiADC object inventory.
  • The API library — the child tables read are recorded as measured for the build they ran on (verdict and field names), with the origin rediscovery-depth:. That evidence is partial, so on its own it never marks a build as harvested.

ℹ️Note

A FortiADC depth capture that was already on the node before SATOM filed it in the deep layer is used by the VS Inspector but is not in the deep layer, in Analysis or in the API library. It enters them only on the next rediscovery with Capture full depth on.

A stop during this pass ends with Stopped during the deep capture, at child-table read 12/40 (<table> ← <parent>). The sweep snapshot was saved; the partial deep capture was discarded and the previous one kept.

Predefined WPPs and the factory catalog#

Every FortiWeb ships the same predefined (factory) WPPs. SATOM keeps them in the Factory catalog, one entry per profile per firmware version, build number and REST API version:

  • The first deep pass on a build reads the predefined WPPs in full and stores them.
  • Later deep passes rebuild a predefined WPP from the catalog, without its sub-table reads, when the appliance's own rows for the profile and every object it names match the entry. Anything that does not match is read in full.
  • An entry is read in full again once it is older than 7 days, and a profile whose entry is ambiguous is always read in full.
  • Switch on Re-read predefined WPPs in full to read every predefined WPP in full now and refresh the catalog. The switch only has an effect together with Capture full WPP + policy depth (slow).

The result line then reports what the catalog did, for example Factory catalog (8.0.3 build 93 · API v2.0): 18 predefined WPP(s) from the factory catalog, 2 read in full. Extra parts appear when they apply: N new in the catalog, N marked ambiguous, N not stored (a read failed) and catalog not updated: with the reason.

CLI capture#

With Also capture the CLI configuration (SSH, slow) on, SATOM opens one read-only SSH session and stores the output of show full-configuration in the configuration vault (see Backups). The CLI-coverage report then compares the catalog against this box as swept. The pass can take up to 5 minutes; the line reads CLI capture (show full-configuration) running… up to 5 min.

When the deep capture is also on, the CLI capture starts together with the deep pass and runs alongside it (one uses SSH, the other REST), so the sweep takes as long as the longer of the two instead of their sum. Without the deep capture, the CLI capture runs after the sweep.

Before anything connects, SATOM decides whether to capture, and the page shows the same decision in advance under the switch:

Reason shown Meaning
the CLI dump is written to the configuration vault, which this user may not write You lack backups.create / backups.restore. The switch is disabled.
the appliance is in maintenance mode, where scheduled collection is suppressed The device is in maintenance mode. The switch is disabled.
a usable dump captured 3.2 h ago is inside the 24 h budget - re-reading the same configuration would only cost the box another 300 s session A readable dump less than 24 hours old exists. The switch stays enabled but no new dump is taken.

The outcome is always one of three, and they are never merged: CLI dump: 680 KB captured, CLI capture skipped: plus the reason, or CLI capture failed: plus the error. A failed CLI pass never fails the sweep, whose snapshot is already saved.

Stop a sweep#

While a sweep runs, a Stop button appears next to Start.

  1. Click Stop. The button changes to Stopping… and the line adds — stopping after the current endpoint… (object… during the deep capture, CLI capture… when the CLI capture is the step still running, step… otherwise).
  2. The sweep checks for the stop request between endpoints, so it ends once the reads in flight return. Reads not yet sent are not sent.

What is kept depends on where the sweep was:

Stopped during Result message What is kept
The sweep Stopped at endpoint 120/310. No snapshot was written; the previous one is unchanged. The previous snapshot. Nothing from this run.
Between the sweep and the deep or CLI pass Stopped before the deep capture. The sweep snapshot was saved; the deep capture was skipped. The new sweep snapshot.
The deep capture Stopped during the deep capture, at object 12/40 (server policy www-shop). The sweep snapshot was saved; the partial deep capture was discarded and the previous one kept. The new sweep snapshot and the previous deep layer. A CLI capture already running alongside the deep pass is allowed to finish (at most 300 s), because one SSH session cannot be cut.
The CLI capture — A CLI capture that has started runs to its end (at most 300 s); there is no safe point to stop one SSH dump.

The Stop button's tooltip says the same: during the endpoint sweep no snapshot is written and the previous one is kept; during the deep pass or the CLI capture the snapshot is already saved and only the remaining work is skipped.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.12.0: a deep rediscovery is much faster. The deep pass walks WPPs first and reads each device object once per sweep (the result line reports N device reads, M reused); the CLI capture runs alongside the deep pass instead of after it, so a Stop during the deep pass lets a CLI capture already running finish; up to 3 reads are kept in flight per FortiWeb on one reused connection pool; predefined WPPs are rebuilt from the Factory catalog, with the new Re-read predefined WPPs in full switch to read them now; and the Stop label names the CLI capture when that is the step still running.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: a FortiADC sweep now stops after one refused login, as FortiWeb already did, and a second sweep can no longer start while the first is still in its deep or CLI pass.

The stopped run shows (by alice) with the user who stopped it, and its job is marked cancelled. Stopping the job from the Jobs dock or the Jobs page has the same effect.

Result#

  • A new latest snapshot (and a copy under its firmware version), unless the sweep was stopped or failed.
  • A harvest record with trigger rediscovery in the device's history; the local cache now holds this configuration.
  • The firmware, model, Hardware/VM type and interfaces of the appliance are updated as described above.
  • The job Discovery · fweb-01 ends as success, cancelled (stopped) or error.
  • Audit entries: appliance.rediscover (with deep and cli flags), appliance.rediscover_stop, and appliance.cli_capture when a dump is stored.

Troubleshooting#

"HTTP 401: the appliance rejected the credentials … Discovery stopped at endpoint 0/310 so it does not lock the admin account out with more failed logins."#

Possible causes - Wrong password or username on the appliance record, or a wrong ADOM in the ADOM (vdom) field. - The device's administrator account is already locked out. - The account's trusted hosts do not include the SATOM node.

This is the one failure that ends a sweep immediately. On a FortiWeb, when an endpoint answers HTTP 401, SATOM asks the device's status once; on a FortiADC, SATOM logs in once more (an expired session is renewed and the read retried). If that is refused too, every further request would be another failed login, and the device locks the account after a few of them — for SATOM and for people using the GUI. So the sweep stops and says at which endpoint. No snapshot was written; the previous one is unchanged.

With parallel reads, a FortiWeb sweep sends several reads at once only after the first status read has proven the credentials. After any 401, no new read is sent until that 401's single re-check has answered, so a lockout in mid-sweep costs at most the reads already in flight plus one re-check (a serial sweep: two failed logins).

Solution 1. Fix the credentials on the appliance's Edit page. 2. If the account is locked, unlock it on the device or wait for the lockout to expire. 3. Test Connection, then start the sweep again.

Verification — Test Connection shows Connection OK and the sweep runs past the first endpoints.

"None of the 310 endpoint(s) answered (310 error(s), e.g. …). No snapshot was written; the previous one is unchanged."#

Possible causes — The device refused every request: an expired or invalid licence (FortiWeb answers -20010 to every read), the host is down, or TLS fails.

Solution — Read the example error. For a TLS failure, see Trust store. For a licence lock, the REST API is unusable but SSH still works: back the device up over SSH from Backups.

"Interrupted — the service restarted while this sweep was running. It wrote no snapshot; run it again."#

Possible causes — SATOM restarted during the sweep.

Solution — Start the sweep again.

"a rediscovery is already running"#

Possible causes — A sweep for this appliance started less than 15 minutes ago and is still in its sweep, deep or CLI phase.

Solution — Wait for it, or stop it. A run whose worker died is marked Interrupted when SATOM restarts.

"Could not stop: this sweep runs on node-b; stop it there"#

Possible causes — In a two-node installation, the sweep runs on the other node.

Solution — Open the page on that node and stop it there.

"Could not stop: no discovery is running"#

Possible causes — The sweep had already finished when Stop was pressed.

The result line says "local cache not updated: …"#

Possible causes — The snapshot was written but storing it in the local cache failed.

Solution — Run the sweep again, or run the scheduled Sync device to local source of truth action for the device. Until then Device health may still say never harvested.

"CLI capture failed: …"#

Possible causes — SSH is closed, the credentials do not work over SSH, or the dump did not look like a complete configuration.

Solution — Check SSH access from the Operator console. The sweep itself is unaffected.

Advanced#

Advanced Other places that start the same sweep
  • After a firmware flash, the upgrade and boot-partition jobs run a full sweep (without deep capture) as their final step. See Firmware upgrade.
  • API versions page (registry area): the card Capture — API catalog + CLI configuration with the button Load API catalog + CLI configuration starts the same sweep with the CLI capture switched on (tick API only (skip the CLI dump) to leave it out). It needs appliances.apply; the CLI half additionally needs a backups permission and is dropped with its reason otherwise. It also reads and stores the running firmware version, and the flash message says whether that worked.
  • The scheduled actions Sync device to local source of truth and Deep capture (full policy/WPP tree) fill the same cache on a schedule, but they are separate actions, not this sweep. See Scheduled actions.
Advanced Parallel reads and environment variables

Set these in the SATOM service environment on the node; they apply to rediscovery only.

Variable Default Effect
SATOM_REDISCOVERY_WORKERS 3 Reads kept in flight per appliance, in the endpoint sweep and in the deep pass. Never above FORTINET_HOST_CONCURRENCY. 1 restores the serial sweep.
FORTINET_HOST_CONCURRENCY 4 Per-host cap on requests in flight that every client obeys, so a sweep cannot take every slot the GUI and the scheduler share.
SATOM_FACTORY_CATALOG on 0 switches the factory catalog off: every predefined WPP is read in full and nothing is stored.
SATOM_FACTORY_REVERIFY_DAYS 7 Age (days, minimum 1) after which a catalog entry is read in full again.

Answers are consumed in plan order, so the snapshot and the progress file are the same as with a serial sweep. The sweep uses one connection pool for all its requests instead of a new TCP and TLS session per request; the pool accepts no cookies. FortiADC sweeps stay serial, because each FortiADC probe logs in to a session of its own.

Advanced Where the sweep's data lives

Progress and snapshots are files on the node, per appliance: a progress file (so every web worker can answer the status poll), the latest snapshot, and a by-version archive with no retention cap. The snapshot is also filed as API-library evidence and refreshes the API matrix used by the registry pages. A library failure is reported in the progress state but never fails the sweep.

Advanced Endpoint verdicts

Absent (errcode -20001 or -3 on FortiWeb) is evidence about the endpoint catalog: the path does not exist on this firmware line. Error is evidence about the device. Absent endpoints are counted separately and are not shown as errors.

Advanced Edge cases
  • The start guard covers every live phase (sweep, deep capture, CLI capture), so a second start cannot clear a Stop request that is still pending for the running sweep. A run marked live for more than 15 minutes is treated as stuck and no longer blocks a start.
  • A stop request pressed after the last phase began is discarded so it cannot stop the next run.
